You are a research group coordinator who needs to document analysis of three foundational papers in language model research. Your task is to analyze three specific papers available in the paper database, create structured notes in your team's Notion workspace, and compile a formal Word report.

The three papers you need to analyze are: "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models" (arXiv ID 2301.07041), "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback" (arXiv ID 2203.11171), and "OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models" (arXiv ID 2205.01068). Use the arXiv and LaTeX analysis tools to retrieve full text and analyze each paper's structure, sections, and key contributions.

For each paper, create a Notion page in your workspace with the paper title as the page title, prefixed with "Paper: ". Include structured notes in the page body covering the paper's main contributions, methodology, and key findings based on the full text you retrieve.

Create a Word document called Paper_Analysis_Report.docx in your workspace. The document should start with a title "Comparative Paper Analysis Report" and include a section for each of the three papers. Each section heading should identify the paper clearly. Within each section, describe the paper's title, key contributions, and methodology. After the three individual sections, include a final section titled "Comparative Analysis" that draws connections between the three papers, discussing how they relate to each other in terms of their contributions to large language model research.

Send an email to research_lead@university.edu with subject "Paper Analysis Report Ready" summarizing what you have done and noting that the Word document and Notion pages are ready for review.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently,

The three fixed-paper source stage is small enough for the main agent; use sub-agents only for the two independent output owners. All research is read-only.

Resolve the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freeze it as `<workspace_root>`, and reject bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. Freeze the three task-specified ID/title slots: `2301.07041 / Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models`, `2203.11171 / Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback`, and `2205.01068 / OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models`.

Issue the arXiv record and arxiv-latex section calls for all three IDs in one native-parallel source response. Verify each returned stable ID/title even if the task's pairing is unusual; do not silently replace a task slot from outside knowledge. For each slot extract title, complete authors when returned, contributions, methodology, findings, section list/count, provenance, and missing/conflict status. Reconcile once and freeze one literal canonical three-paper packet; the Notion pages, Word report, and email consume this exact packet without re-researching or recomputing claims.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel as individual Agent calls:

   1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Notion owner: search exact titles `Paper: <canonical title>`; reuse one exact match, create at most one page on zero matches, and block on duplicates. Own all three pages in one agent so parent IDs and idempotency stay consistent. Each page must contain substantive Contribution, Methodology, and Findings blocks copied from the canonical packet. Read all three pages back and return IDs, exact titles, stable-ID coverage, and block validation. Do not write the Word file or email.
   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Word owner: create `<workspace_root>/Paper_Analysis_Report.docx` exactly once, preferably atomically with `python-docx`, with the required report title, one clearly headed section per canonical paper, and a final Comparative Analysis grounded only in those records. Read it back and return path, heading order, exact paper/title coverage, and validation. Do not modify Notion or email.

In the same response that launches Wave 1, the main agent paginates Sent search for exact To `research_lead@university.edu` and Subject `Paper Analysis Report Ready`, reading every candidate. After both outputs return, send exactly once only if no exact match exists, mentioning the verified Word filename and the three verified Notion page titles/IDs. Never retry an ambiguous send. Accept only after all pages, the document, and exactly one message read back against the canonical packet.

You are planning a multi-system research-coordination task. Produce an ordered, actionable plan (subtasks with dispatch decision: self / explore / coder, and dependency info: parallelizable vs. sequential). Do NOT execute the task — only plan.

TASK DESCRIPTION (from the coordinator):
The coordinator must analyze three foundational LLM papers and produce three deliverables:

1. ANALYSIS: Retrieve full text / structure for each of these three papers (available in the arXiv paper database and LaTeX analysis tools):
   - "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models" (arXiv 2301.07041)
   - "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback" (arXiv 2203.11171)
   - "OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models" (arXiv 2205.01068)
   For each paper, analyze sections/structure and extract: main contributions, methodology, key findings.

2. NOTION: Create one Notion page per paper, page title = "Paper: <paper title>", in the team's Notion workspace. Page body must contain structured notes covering main contributions, methodology, key findings based on full text retrieved.

3. WORD: Create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/Paper_Analysis_Report.docx starting with title "Comparative Paper Analysis Report", then a section per paper (heading identifying each paper clearly) describing title, key contributions, methodology. Finally a section titled "Comparative Analysis" drawing connections among the three papers regarding their contributions to large language model research.

4. EMAIL: Send email to research_lead@university.edu, subject "Paper Analysis Report Ready", summarizing what was done and noting the Word document and Notion pages are ready for review.

ENVIRONMENT / TOOLS:
- Workspace (writable) dir: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace
- arXiv tools: mcp__arxiv_local__list_papers, mcp__arxiv_local__search_papers, mcp__arxiv_local__download_paper, mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper; also mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_abstract, mcp__arxiv-latex__list_paper_sections, mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section, mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt (flattened LaTeX).
- Notion tools: mcp__notion__API-post-search (find workspace/parent page), mcp__notion__API-post-page (create pages), mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children (append body blocks).
- Word tools: mcp__word__create_document, mcp__word__add_heading, mcp__word__add_paragraph, mcp__word__get_document_text (verify), etc.
- Email tools: mcp__emails__send_email, mcp__emails__check_connection.

CONSTRAINTS:
- The plan must include a step to locate the Notion parent page/workspace before creating pages (e.g., search Notion for an appropriate parent page), and a step to verify each deliverable (read back Notion page, read docx text, confirm email sent).
- Papers must be analyzed from actual retrieved content (do not rely on memory).
- Suggest parallelization: the three paper analyses are independent and parallelizable (suggest AgentSwarm or parallel coder agents); Word doc build depends on the analyses; Notion page creation depends on analyses and on locating the Notion parent; email is last.
- Deliverable: ordered subtask list, each with dispatch decision, dependencies, and acceptance criteria. Keep it concise and directly executable.

You are analyzing a foundational large language model (LLM) research paper for a research-group coordinator. The paper to analyze is: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (arXiv ID 2301.07041)

GOAL: Produce a thorough, evidence-based structural analysis of this paper using the arXiv retrieval tools, and save it as a Markdown notes file in the shared workspace. Do NOT rely on prior knowledge — retrieve the actual paper content.

STEPS:
1. Determine the arXiv ID from the paper name given above.
2. Retrieve full text: call mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper with paper_id = the arXiv ID (e.g. "2301.07041"). This returns the full paper in markdown.
3. Also use the LaTeX analysis tools to verify structure and get precise math where useful: mcp__arxiv-latex__list_paper_sections (arXiv ID without version suffix), mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_section (e.g. section_path "1" or "2.1" or "Introduction"), and if needed mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_prompt for flattened LaTeX. Fetch the abstract via mcp__arxiv-latex__get_paper_abstract.
4. Extract the following structured analysis from the retrieved content:
   - Exact paper title, first authors (up to 3), arXiv ID, publication/abstract summary (1-2 sentences)
   - MAIN CONTRIBUTIONS: 3-5 bullets grounded in the paper text
   - METHODOLOGY: a detailed paragraph(s) describing how the work was done (models, datasets, training setup, evaluation, techniques)
   - KEY FINDINGS: 3-5 bullets with the most important quantitative/qualitative results
   - NOTABLE SECTIONS: list of the paper's major section headings (from list_paper_sections)
5. Save the analysis to this exact path (create the notes directory first with mcp__filesystem__create_directory if needed): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/notes/analysis_<arXivID>.md
   Use mcp__filesystem__write_file. The file should be well-structured Markdown with clear headings (# Paper Title, ## Main Contributions, ## Methodology, ## Key Findings, ## Notable Sections).

DELIVERABLE / ACCEPTANCE: The notes file exists at the specified path with all five sections populated from retrieved content. In your final summary, report: the file path you wrote, a 6-10 line digest of the analysis (title, top contributions, methodology essence, top findings) — this digest will be relayed to downstream tasks. Do not include the full file contents in your summary.

You are building a formal Word report for a research group coordinator using the Word document MCP tools. Work ONLY inside /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace (this is the writable workspace).

CONTEXT: Three foundational LLM papers were analyzed; structured notes exist at:
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/notes/analysis_2301.07041.md  (Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models)
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/notes/analysis_2203.11171.md  (Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback / InstructGPT)
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/notes/analysis_2205.01068.md  (OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models)

Read all three notes files first (mcp__filesystem__read_multiple_files or read_text_file) to get accurate content — do not rely on memory.

TASK: Create the file Paper_Analysis_Report.docx at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/Paper_Analysis_Report.docx with the following structure, using the Word tools (mcp__word__*):

1. create_document with filename = the full path above (set title metadata "Comparative Paper Analysis Report" if supported).
2. Add a title heading "Comparative Paper Analysis Report" (Heading 1 / title style).
3. Then a section for EACH paper (use Heading 1 or Heading 2 for each section heading, make it clearly identify the paper — include the paper title and arXiv ID). Within each paper's section, add paragraphs describing:
   - The paper's title (and authors/arXiv ID)
   - Key contributions (use the notes' Main Contributions)
   - Methodology (use the notes' Methodology)
   Write flowing paragraphs (you may use bold labels like "Title:", "Key Contributions:", "Methodology:" as separate short paragraphs or inline — your choice, keep it clean and professional).
   Section order: 1) Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (arXiv 2301.07041), 2) Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback (arXiv 2203.11171), 3) OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models (arXiv 2205.01068).
4. After the three paper sections, add a final section with heading exactly "Comparative Analysis" (Heading 1 or 2). Write 2-3 paragraphs drawing connections among the three papers: e.g., Scaling Laws provides the empirical foundation (power-law loss vs. model size, data, compute) guiding how to allocate compute and why scale matters; OPT operationalizes scaling by openly reproducing a 175B-parameter GPT-3-class model, democratizing frontier-scale research; InstructGPT shows that beyond scale, alignment via RLHF lets a much smaller model (1.3B) beat a 100x larger base model (GPT-3 175B) at instruction following. Together they represent three complementary axes of LLM research — predictive scaling theory, open large-scale reproduction, and human-feedback alignment — that jointly shaped the modern LLM paradigm.
5. Verify the document by calling mcp__word__get_document_text on the final file and confirm all required headings/sections are present with non-empty content.

ACCEPTANCE: Paper_Analysis_Report.docx exists at the exact path; get_document_text confirms the title, three paper sections with content, and the "Comparative Analysis" section. Report back: the final file path and a brief confirmation of the verified structure (list the headings you confirmed).

CONTEXT: Three foundational LLM papers were analyzed; structured notes exist at:
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/notes/analysis_2301.07041.md  (paper title: "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models", arXiv 2301.07041)
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/notes/analysis_2203.11171.md  (paper title: "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback", arXiv 2203.11171)
- /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-analysis-notion-word/workspace/notes/analysis_2205.01068.md  (paper title: "OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models", arXiv 2205.01068)

Read all three notes files first (mcp__filesystem__read_multiple_files or read_text_file) — use their actual content, do not rely on memory.

TASK: Create one Notion page per paper, using mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent = {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true} and properties containing the title. The page title MUST be exactly "Paper: <paper title>" (e.g., "Paper: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models").

For each page's body, append structured notes using mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children (block_id = the new page id returned by API-post-page). The body should contain:
- A heading_2 (or paragraph) "Main Contributions" followed by bulleted_list_item blocks for each contribution from the notes file.
- A heading_2 "Methodology" followed by paragraph block(s) summarizing the methodology from the notes file.
- A heading_2 "Key Findings" followed by bulleted_list_item blocks for each key finding.
- Optionally a heading_2 "Notable Sections" with bulleted list items for the sections.
Use the notes' actual content for all of this. Suggested page title mapping:
1. "Paper: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models" (from analysis_2301.07041.md)
2. "Paper: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback" (from analysis_2203.11171.md)
3. "Paper: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models" (from analysis_2205.01068.md)

VERIFICATION: For each of the three pages, call mcp__notion__API-retrieve-a-page (confirm title) and mcp__notion__API-get-block-children (confirm body blocks exist and contain expected content). 

ACCEPTANCE: Three Notion pages exist with exact titles "Paper: <paper title>" and bodies containing Main Contributions / Methodology / Key Findings blocks populated from the notes. Report back: the page IDs + URLs (if returned) for all three pages and a summary of verified titles and block counts.
